title: Dockerfiles and Container Development
description: Write Dockerfiles to build optimized container images and use Docker commands to build, run, and manage containers locally.

data.text: A Dockerfile is a text file that defines the steps to build a container image. Each instruction creates a layer in the image. Understanding Dockerfiles is essential for building efficient, secure containers.

data.title: Dockerfile - .NET App
data.content:
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY *.csproj ./
RUN dotnet restore
COPY . .
RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o /app/publish

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/publish .
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "MyApp.dll"]

data.text: Multi-stage builds use a build image to compile the application, then copy only the published output to a smaller runtime image. This dramatically reduces the final image size.

data.title: Minimize Image Layers
data.text: Combine related RUN commands with && to reduce layers. Each instruction adds a layer, and fewer layers mean smaller images and faster builds.

data.title: Dockerfile - Optimized with Combined Commands
data.content:
# Single RUN layer for dependencies
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        curl \
        git && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

data.title: Terminal - Common Docker Commands
data.content:
# Build an image
docker build -t myapp:1.0 .

# Run a container
docker run -d -p 8080:8080 --name myapp myapp:1.0

# List running containers
docker ps

# View logs
docker logs myapp

# Stop and remove
docker rm -f myapp

# Push to a registry
docker tag myapp:1.0 myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:1.0
docker push myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:1.0

data.title: Build a Container Image
data.description: Create a Dockerfile for a simple ASP.NET Core app and build it locally.
steps: Create a new ASP.NET Core Web API project
Write a Dockerfile using a multi-stage build
Build the image with `docker build -t myapi .`
Run the container and test the API at localhost:8080
data.expectedOutcome: The API is accessible inside the running container.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Dockerfiles define how to build a container image
Each Dockerfile instruction creates a new layer
docker build, run, push, and pull are core commands
data.takeaway: Master Dockerfiles to build efficient, production-ready container images.
